answers.falsifier: a journal record whose proven_by carries backslashes reads back from proven_by_since_buildme as the posix path ; the crossing writes proven_by with forward slashes, so a Windows crossing stores no backslash
answers.how: In cairn/tools/base/crossings.py _norm_proof replaces backslashes with forward slashes before the repo-prefix strip (so a backslash absolute path under the repo also strips). In cairn/tools/base/cross.py the proven_by list is written through the same posix conversion. Red-first proof cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_a_crossing_proven_by_is_posix.py feeds a fixture journal record carrying a backslash path and asserts the posix path back, and calls the crossing's write path and asserts no backslash is stored.
answers.title: a crossing's proven_by is a posix path, written and read
answers.traces_to: Law 3 and Law 8: a proof path a Linux reader cannot match is evidence no peer can lean on; Law 7: the stored record is kept as written, the reader fixes the reading.
answers.what: proven_by_since_buildme returns posix paths whatever separator the journal stored, and the crossing writes proven_by with forward slashes.
